sections.html:
Owners in a hurry usually sell straight to a cash buyer, while owners with time often go through an agent. A direct sale skips showings, a buyer's loan and an appraisal, so closing depends mostly on clear title.

  • Cash buyer: suits inherited houses, tenant-occupied rentals, deferred repairs and foreclosure dates.
  • Agent: suits a house in good repair and a seller with room in the schedule.
  • By owner: suits someone comfortable with contracts and buyer screening.

Cleburne is the Johnson County seat, and the county appraisal district keeps its office in the city.

Cleburne sits on U.S. Highway 67, thirty miles south of Fort Worth. It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867, when the county needed a central seat to replace Buchanan, and it incorporated in May 1871. A rail line through town opened in 1881, and the Santa Fe built its central machine shops here in 1898 and 1899. That railroad past explains why older neighborhoods near the center look different from newer Dallas-Fort Worth suburbs, and why a buyer may ask about the age of wiring and plumbing in an older house.

sections.h2: Where to get Cleburne property values
sections.html:
Values come from the Central Appraisal District of Johnson County at 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne. Hours are 8:00am to 4:30pm on weekdays, with a drop box in the front door, and the phone is (817) 648-3000. The district was upgrading its software in 2026, so check any exemption on your account with the office itself instead of relying on a screen.

sections.h2: Questions about value or a protest
sections.html:
The district also links a Taxpayer Liaison Officer, a role the Tax Code requires in counties with populations above 120,000, who helps taxpayers with access to district functions.

An owner can ask the district to deliver notices electronically, since Tax Code Section 1.085(a-1) requires a tax official to honor that request. That helps a seller who has moved out but still gets the property's notices at the old address.

sections.h2: Exemptions for a Cleburne homeowner or buyer
sections.html:
School districts give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with an additional $60,000 for owners who are older or disabled. Disabled veteran brackets run from $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a veteran rated 100 percent disabled can get a total exemption on a homestead.

File with the appraisal district before May 1. A buyer who moves in after January 1 can often claim the exemption for the rest of that year if the seller never held it. Your own exemption stays with you, so a buyer applies for theirs.

Ask the City of Cleburne's building inspections office whether any permit on your address is open or unfinished, and request the record in writing so you can hand it to the title company.

If there is an unfinished project, the cleanest fix is to finish and close the permit. If you can't, say so in writing to any buyer and let them decide how to price it. Many buyers purchase as-is, and sellers disclose known problems.

Texas lenders with a power of sale in the deed of trust can foreclose at a courthouse auction without suing, which for a Cleburne house means Johnson County. The borrower has 20 days from receiving the default notice to catch up.

The sale notice must reach the borrower at least 21 days ahead and also be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. If the lender sues afterward over a shortfall, the suit must come within two years. Selling before the auction may protect your equity, so act early if a notice has arrived.

Each of these has its own Texas rule.

  • Inherited: four years to probate a will; a muniment of title can move title when no administration is needed; a small estate affidavit requires $75,000 or less outside homestead and exempt property, plus agreement among all heirs.
  • Tenant: 3 days of written notice, a justice court filing, then a 6-day wait after judgment before a writ of possession; an appeal to county court is due within 5 days.

Tell the buyer about each issue at the start. The title company will want proof of authority to sell, such as a court order or recorded affidavit.

faqs.q: Where is the Johnson County appraisal district office?
faqs.a: At 109 N. Main St. in Cleburne, open weekdays 8:00am to 4:30pm, phone (817) 648-3000. A drop box sits in the front door.

faqs.q: How old is the city of Cleburne?
faqs.a: It became a permanent settlement on March 23, 1867 and incorporated in May 1871. It replaced Buchanan as the Johnson County seat.

faqs.q: What is the school homestead exemption in Texas?
faqs.a: School districts exempt $140,000, with an additional $60,000 for owners who are older or disabled.

faqs.q: How much notice comes before a Texas foreclosure auction?
faqs.a: At least 21 days, and only after the 20-day reinstatement window that follows the default notice. Auctions happen on first Tuesdays.

faqs.q: Does a Cleburne house with repairs still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Many buyers purchase as-is, and sellers disclose known problems. An open permit or code issue is the item most likely to need attention before closing, so ask Building Inspections what is on file.
